summary: Verified the manager_name fallback bug fix in processing.py and the speaker_colors _ensure_dict fix in review.py. All 6 tests passed (4 API + 2 code-level).
critical_code_review_comments: All 3 occurrences of manager_name in processing.py (lines 207, 479, 580) correctly use: sign_off_manager_name OR created_by_name OR 'Manager'
review.py line 192: speaker_colors correctly processed via _ensure_dict() to prevent raw-string JSONB issues
meetings.py: When sign_off_manager_id is absent, created_by_name is set to current_user['name'] on INSERT — the fallback in processing.py will correctly use this value
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up one TEST_FallbackManager Meeting via API
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix fully verified: processing.py manager_name fallback (sign_off_manager_name → created_by_name → 'Manager') confirmed at all 3 call sites. review.py speaker_colors _ensure_dict fix confirmed. API verified: admin creating a meeting without sign_off_manager_id results in sign_off_manager_name=null and created_by_name=admin's actual name persisted in DB.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: processing.py previously used sign_off_manager_name directly with no fallback. When a meeting creator (e.g. Daniel Okafor) did not explicitly set themselves as sign_off_manager, sign_off_manager_name was null, so the literal string 'Manager' was hardcoded as the diarization speaker label. Fix: all 3 locations now use `meeting.get('sign_off_manager_name') or meeting.get('created_by_name') or 'Manager'`, so the creator's name is always used as fallback.
